correctness.rationale: Changing the focal action changes shared benefit iff exactly one of n-1 coplayers cooperates; gain is B(n-1)x(1-x)^(n-2)-C. Under experienced mixture p of n2 and 1-p of n4 this yields H_p(x)=px+3(1-p)x(1-x)^2 and flow B*x(1-x)*(H_p(x)-kappa). H_p derivative is quadratic 9(1-p)x^2-12(1-p)x+(3-2p), with two simple interior turning points iff 0<p<1/2; levels strictly between the local minimum and min(local max,H_p(1)=p) have exactly three interior roots, alternating unstable-stable-unstable, and 0/1 stable. Else cannot have three distinct attracting states under stated nondegenerate assumptions. Fixed n gain is unimodal; any mixture sizes <=3 is quadratic and has at most two interior roots, so max size4 sharp. Independent exact symbolic factorization p=11/23,kappa=10/23 gives (2x-1)(3x-2)(6x-5)/23, stable 0,2/3,1, repelling 1/2,5/6; experienced p differs from group-count probabilities (11/17,6/17). Strict inequalities exclude degenerate/nonhyperbolic boundaries.

value.rationale: Group-size heterogeneity can create a mixed-cooperation attracting state simultaneously with stable total defection and stable total cooperation. The sharp minimal maximum group size 4, full open parameter window, and exact rational witness define a substantive bifurcation boundary in a canonical two-helper public-goods model without adding strategies or punishment. The gain identity alone is classical; the complete three-attractor classification is the value contribution.

final_claim: For a two-helper threshold public-good replicator game with experienced group sizes two/four, exactly three attracting states occur iff the explicit two-critical-point and strict cost window hold; size four is the minimal maximum group size for this mechanism.
limitations: Two-helper exactly, two strategies, constant B>0 and 0<C<B, size-two and size-four experienced probabilities fixed.
